## {#today .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.todaymeta}
A one-day course on open science, in four parts of 90 minutes, on the housing-audit case
:::

:::: {.todaybox}
::: {.nonincremental .fs-85}
1. Credibility and open research – the crisis, the three Rs, and where open research keeps its materials
2. The claim and its estimand – the paper, the five analysts, and the question behind the claim
3. Reproduction – one of the five reanalyses reproduced, and what a reproduction needs
4. Replication and preregistration – the new audit, and what a preregistration fixes

::: {.todaymeta}
Work along in the browser lab, solo or in pairs, or in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) if you have installed the workspace
:::

::: notes
Welcome – good to have you here. A full day in four parts of ninety minutes, and today open research is in the foreground. The first part asks what a claim in social science is for, why people say the field is in crisis, and what open research proposes as a remedy, down to the archives and registries where its materials are kept. The second goes inside one published experiment, in which a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing, and asks what question its claim answers. In the third you reproduce one of the five independent reanalyses of that claim, whichever you choose, and we work out what a reproduction needs besides data and code. And in the fourth we meet the new study that tested the claim again, read its preregistration, and you fill in a preregistration of your own.
:::
